items.title: Knot exterior
items.statement:
Assume countable choice, as required for the smooth normal-bundle structure in the tubular-neighbourhood interface. Let $K:S^1\to S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and let $\nu(K)=TS^3|_K/TK$ be its quotient normal bundle. Equip $\nu(K)$ with a chosen smooth fibre norm $\|\cdot\|$. Let $\Phi:\Omega\to S^3$ be a tubular-neighbourhood map from an open neighbourhood $\Omega$ of the zero section in $\nu(K)$ that restricts to the inclusion of $K$. For $\epsilon>0$, define the closed disk subbundle
$$
D_\epsilon\nu(K):=\{v\in\nu(K):\|v\|\le\epsilon\}.
$$
Choose $\epsilon$ so that $D_\epsilon\nu(K)\subseteq\Omega$, and set $N(K)=\Phi(D_\epsilon\nu(K))$. The fibre norm, tubular map, and radius are part of the chosen tubular data. The **exterior** of this chosen tube is
$$
E_K:=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}_{S^3}N(K).
$$
Retain its boundary $T_K:=\partial E_K=\partial N(K)$, orient $E_K$ by restriction of the fixed orientation of $S^3$, and orient $T_K$ as the boundary of $E_K$. The choice of tubular map and radius is part of the input to this definition.

references.title: Alessia Cattabriga and Stefano Francaviglia, Knot Theory and Applications: Lecture Notes

items.strategy: Definition for a supplied tube; later local lemmas establish existence, compactness, the boundary torus, and tube-independence claims actually used on this page.

items.title: The oriented normal bundle of a knot is trivial
items.statement:
For every smooth oriented embedding $K:S^1	o S^3$, let $
u_K=K^*TS^3/dK(TS^1)$ be the quotient normal bundle. Orient its two-dimensional fibres so that a positive tangent to $K$ followed by a positive basis of the normal fibre gives the fixed orientation of $S^3$. Then $
u_K$ admits a smooth orientation-preserving bundle isomorphism $
u_K\cong K	imes\mathbb R^2$.

references.title: Danny Calegari, Introduction to Knot Theory
Alessia Cattabriga and Stefano Francaviglia, Knot Theory and Applications: Lecture Notes
references.locator: Section 4.4, meridian and peripheral orientation conventions

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Vector Bundles and K-Theory
references.locator: Section 1.2, Proposition 1.14 and the discussion of oriented bundles over $S^1$, printed pp. 25-26

items.strategy: Direct clutching argument: cut S^1 into an interval, trivialize the oriented rank-two bundle there, and remove the endpoint gluing using path-connectedness of GL+(2,R). The proof is choice-free.

items.title: Meridian and preferred longitude
items.statement: Assume countable choice as in the chosen tubular-neighbourhood data. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot with chosen exterior $E_K$ and boundary torus $T_K=\partial E_K$, and let $p:T_K\to K$ be the projection of the chosen normal-disk tube. Orient each normal disk so that its positive tangent direction followed by its oriented normal basis agrees with the orientation of $S^3$. A **meridian** $\mu$ is the oriented boundary of one such normal disk. A **degree-one parallel curve** is a simple closed curve $\lambda$ in $T_K$ for which $p|_\lambda:\lambda\to K$ has degree $+1$. A **preferred longitude** is a degree-one parallel curve satisfying $i_*[\lambda]=0$ in $H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z)$, where $i:T_K\hookrightarrow E_K$ is inclusion. This is a condition on a curve; this definition alone asserts neither existence nor uniqueness. Reversing the orientation of $K$ reverses the orientations of both $\mu$ and any degree-one parallel curve. If a subgroup $P\le\pi_1(E_K,x)$ is specified using a path from $x$ to $T_K$, record it only up to replacing it by $gPg^{-1}$ for $g\in\pi_1(E_K,x)$.

references.title: Alessia Cattabriga and Stefano Francaviglia, Knot Theory and Applications: Lecture Notes
references.locator: Section 4.4, meridian, longitude, and peripheral-system conventions

references.title: Danny Calegari, Introduction to Knot Theory

items.strategy: Define the meridian from the oriented normal disk and the longitude as a degree-one boundary-parallel zero-homology condition. Leave existence and uniqueness to the later theorem, avoiding a circular definition.

items.title: Tubular exterior and boundary torus
items.statement: Assume countable choice. For every smooth oriented knot $K$ in $S^3$, there are an oriented normal-bundle trivialization, a tubular map $\Phi$ defined on an open neighbourhood containing $S^1\times D^2_{2\epsilon}$ for some $\epsilon>0$, and a closed tubular neighbourhood $N(K)=\Phi(S^1\times D^2_\epsilon)$. This $N(K)$ is diffeomorphic to $S^1\times D^2$, its boundary $T_K$ is diffeomorphic to $S^1\times S^1$, and its exterior $E_K=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$ is a compact smooth oriented three-manifold with boundary $T_K$. The open complement $S^3\setminus K$ strongly deformation retracts onto $E_K$.

references.title: Alessia Cattabriga and Stefano Francaviglia, Knot Theory and Applications: Lecture Notes
references.locator: Section 4.1, compact exterior and boundary torus

items.strategy: Use the published smooth tubular-neighbourhood theorem under its exact AC_omega hypothesis, the local oriented normal trivialization, compactness of S^1 to choose a uniform disk radius, and radial retraction in the punctured disk fibres.

items.title: The knot exterior has a peripheral torus basis
items.statement: Assume countable choice. For a smooth oriented knot with a chosen product tubular neighbourhood $N(K)\cong S^1\times D^2$, let $\mu$ be the positive fibre meridian and let $\sigma$ be the product section $s\mapsto(s,1)$ of $T_K=\partial N(K)\cong S^1\times S^1$. Then $T_K=\partial E_K$ is a torus and $[\mu],[\sigma]$ form a basis of $H_1(T_K;\mathbb Z)$. The curve $\sigma$ is a product section; this statement does not assert that it is the preferred zero-homology longitude.

references.title: Alessia Cattabriga and Stefano Francaviglia, Knot Theory and Applications: Lecture Notes
Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology
references.locator: Section 2.2, Example 2.36, cellular homology of closed orientable surfaces

items.strategy: Identify the boundary with S^1 x S^1 and compute its first homology from its one-vertex, two-edge, one-face CW structure; the commutator attaching map has zero cellular boundary.

items.title: Homology and preferred longitude of a knot exterior
items.statement:
Assume countable choice. Let $K:S^1	o S^3$ be a smooth oriented embedding and write its quotient normal bundle as $
u_K=K^*TS^3/dK(TS^1)$. Choose an orientation-preserving trivialization $
u_K\cong S^1	imes\mathbb R^2$ and a tubular map $\Phi:\Omega	o S^3$, meaning a smooth embedding from an open neighbourhood $\Omega\subseteq
u_K$ of the zero section onto an open neighbourhood of $K(S^1)$ with $\Phi(s,0)=K(s)$, such that in these product coordinates $\Omega$ contains $S^1	imes D^2_{2\epsilon}$ for some $\epsilon>0$. Here $D^2_r=\{z\in\mathbb R^2:\|z\|\le r\}$ uses the product Euclidean norm induced by the chosen trivialization. Set $N(K)=\Phi(S^1	imes D^2_\epsilon)$, $E_K=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$, $T_K=\partial E_K$, and let $i:T_K\hookrightarrow E_K$ be inclusion, $p:T_K	o S^1$ the product projection, and $\mu$ the positive boundary of a normal disk, using the normal-plane orientation determined by the orientations of $K$ and $S^3$. A class is primitive if it is not $m$ times another class for any integer $|m|>1$. Then $H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z$ is generated by $[\mu]$. The kernel of $i_*:H_1(T_K;\mathbb Z)	o H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z)$ is a primitive rank-one direct summand generated by a unique class $[\lambda]$ with $p_*[\lambda]=1\in H_1(S^1;\mathbb Z)$. It has a simple closed representative, is the preferred longitude, and $([\mu],[\lambda])$ is a basis of $H_1(T_K;\mathbb Z)$.

references.title: Alessia Cattabriga and Stefano Francaviglia, Knot Theory and Applications: Lecture Notes
references.locator: Sections 4.1 and 4.4, compact exterior and peripheral systems

references.title: Danny Calegari, Introduction to Knot Theory
references.locator: Section 3.3, meridian convention and linking context, pp. 26-30

items.strategy: Use an open tubular collar cover and radial deformation retractions, then Mayer-Vietoris with H2(S3)=H1(S3)=0. Prove the meridian generator by the unimodular inclusion matrix and the unique primitive kernel longitude by an integral change of basis.

title: Knot exteriors and peripheral systems — Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: Worked case: the unknot exterior
items.statement: Assume countable choice. Give the unit sphere $S^3=\{(z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb C^2:|z_1|^2+|z_2|^2=1\}$ its standard boundary orientation, and orient the standard unknot $U(t)=(e^{2\pi it},0)$ by increasing $t\in\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$. For $r>0$, write $D^2_r=\{w\in\mathbb C:|w|\le r\}$. Choose the closed tubular neighbourhood $N(U)=\{(z_1,z_2)\in S^3:|z_2|\le 1/\sqrt2\}$, using the norm $|w|$ on its normal disk fibres. Its exterior $E_U=\{(z_1,z_2)\in S^3:|z_2|\ge 1/\sqrt2\}$ is a solid torus diffeomorphic to $D^2_{1/\sqrt2}\times S^1$. On its boundary, the positive meridian is the phase loop in $z_2$, while the preferred longitude has representative $t\mapsto(e^{2\pi it}/\sqrt2,e^{i\theta_0}/\sqrt2)$ for fixed $\theta_0$; consequently $H_1(E_U;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z$ is generated by $[\mu]$ and $[\lambda]=0$.

references.title: Alessia Cattabriga and Stefano Francaviglia, Knot Theory and Applications: Lecture Notes

items.strategy: Compute an explicit standard splitting of the unit three-sphere into two solid tori, then identify the meridian and preferred longitude in those product coordinates.

items.title: An arbitrary parallel push-off need not be preferred
items.statement: Assume countable choice. For every smooth oriented knot $K$ with a chosen product tubular neighbourhood $N(K)\cong S^1\times D^2$ using its product Euclidean fibre norm, define its exterior by $E_K=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$ and its boundary torus by $T_K=\partial E_K$. Let $i:T_K\hookrightarrow E_K$ be inclusion and let $p:T_K\to S^1$ be the product projection to the oriented core. Every primitive class $c\in H_1(T_K;\mathbb Z)$ with $p_*c=1\in H_1(S^1;\mathbb Z)$ is in $\ker i_*$. Here primitive means that $c$ is not an integer multiple $m d$ of another class with $|m|>1$.

references.title: Alessia Cattabriga and Stefano Francaviglia, Knot Theory and Applications: Lecture Notes
references.locator: Remark 4.4.4 and the peripheral basis discussion, Section 4.4

items.strategy: Refute the universal claim by the primitive class [lambda]+[mu]; its core projection has degree one, but its exterior image is the nonzero meridian generator.
